questions.question: The trailer hand valve:

options.text: Should always be used for parking.
Should only be used for parking on a downgrade.
Should never be used for parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should never be used for parking.
questions.explanation: Do not use the trailer hand valve for parking. It can release air pressure from the brake system and cause the brakes to fail. Use the parking brake or wheel chocks instead.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Move quickly before other vehicles get into the lane you wish to occupy.
Move slowly, in case another vehicle is in the lane you wish to occupy.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move slowly, in case another vehicle is in the lane you wish to occupy.
questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly. This gives other drivers time to move or warn you with their horn. Always use your turn signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that you could block other vehicles, you should:

options.text: Drive with your emergency flashers activated.
Wave an arm out of your window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with your emergency flashers activated.
questions.explanation: When driving slowly, use your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. Check that local laws allow this.

questions.question: When loading corrosive materials, you should not:
questions.explanation: Load corrosive containers one at a time by hand. Keep them upright. Do not drop or roll the containers.

questions.question: When uncoupling a trailer, the landing gear should be:
questions.explanation: Always raise the landing gear completely before driving. When uncoupling, lower the landing gear until it is firmly on the ground. If the trailer is loaded, turn the crank a few more times to remove some weight from the trailer.

questions.question: You should check and adjust your mirrors:
questions.explanation: Check and adjust your mirrors before you start driving. Your posture changes day to day, and your mirrors may need adjustment.

questions.question: You may be an aggressive driver if you:

options.text: Slow down and maintain a reasonable following distance.
Make hand gestures that could anger other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make hand gestures that could anger other drivers.
questions.explanation: Avoid aggressive driving by planning for delays, maintaining safe distance from other vehicles, and not making hand gestures that upset other drivers.

questions.question: If a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, the hazardous materials may need to be:

options.text: Circled by a pen or marker.

questions.explanation: When a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, hazardous materials must be marked in one of three ways: listed first, highlighted in a contrasting color, or marked with an "X" in the "HM" column.

questions.question: When loading a tank, space must be left for outage. What is outage?

options.text: A place for luggage and personal items

questions.explanation: Liquids expand when heated. A tank must have extra empty space so the liquid can expand safely. This extra space is called outage.

questions.question: Hazardous materials placards are usually shaped like:
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: When you walk up to your vehicle, you should check that:

options.text: The vehicle is not parked too close to other vehicles.
There are no puddles under the vehicle that show a leak.
The vehicle is parked in the right spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are no puddles under the vehicle that show a leak.
questions.explanation: Before you inspect your vehicle, look at its general condition. Check that it is not damaged or leaning. Look under the vehicle for fresh leaks. Look around the vehicle for hazards like people, other vehicles, or low-hanging wires or tree limbs.

questions.question: While driving, you should:

options.text: Think ahead about how to handle any dangerous situation.
Focus only on your own driving and ignore other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Think ahead about how to handle any dangerous situation.
questions.explanation: While driving, always watch the road ahead for hazards. Have a plan to deal with any dangers that might happen.

questions.question: Hazardous materials shipping papers must not be kept:

options.text: In a pouch on the driver's door.
In a pouch on the passenger's door.
Within reach of the driver while wearing a seat belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a pouch on the passenger's door.
questions.explanation: Shipping papers must be easy to grab in an emergency. While driving, keep papers in a pouch on the driver's door or in clear view and within reach while your seat belt is on. You can keep papers on the driver's seat when you are out of the vehicle.

questions.question: Before loading or unloading flammable liquids, the engine should be:
questions.explanation: Before loading or unloading a tank with flammable liquids, turn off the engine. The only exception is if you need the engine running to operate a pump. Ground the tank before you open the filling hole. Keep it grounded until after you close the filling hole.

questions.question: If you are not sure your vehicle can fit safely under a bridge, you should:

options.text: Swerve as you pass under the bridge.

questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under an overhead object safely, slow down. Try to find an alternate route if possible.

questions.question: Before opening trailer doors during a small truck fire, you should:

options.text: Feel the doors to see if they are hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel the doors to see if they are hot.
questions.explanation: If your truck is on fire, feel the doors before opening them to see if they are hot. Hot doors may mean the cargo is on fire. Keep the doors closed if there is a cargo fire.

questions.question: If oil and water build up in your air tanks, the brakes:
questions.explanation: Drain air tanks every day to remove water and oil. Too much oil and water in the air tanks can hurt how well your brakes work.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, do not park the vehicle:

options.text: For only short periods of time.

questions.explanation: Do not park a vehicle carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building. Do not park within five feet of the road. Park only for short periods when needed for vehicle operation.

questions.question: When checking the engine, you should check everything except:

options.text: The coolant level in the radiator.

questions.explanation: When you check the engine, look at the oil level, radiator coolant level and hose condition, power steering fluid level and hose condition, windshield washer fluid level, battery connections and fluid level, automatic transmission fluid level, and belt condition. Also check for leaks and damaged wiring.

questions.question: During an inspection, the most important thing to check on a tank vehicle is:
questions.explanation: When you inspect any tank, check for leaks first. Transporting gas or liquid in a leaking tank is against the law.
